eliyah-rabbah:1:_: [1] [Levush] It is not reshut ha-rabbim, etc. And regarding when one throws from reshut ha-yachid to reshut ha-rabbim — Taz distinguishes between open to reshut ha-rabbim where the public presses within it that he is not liable — see there; and Bach and Magen Avraham imply that in any case he is liable; and see beginning of siman 345:
eliyah-rabbah:2:_: [2] [Levush] Mashehu from here, etc. In Shulchan Aruch he wrote a tefach from here — for the remainder of the wall is less than a pas with mashehu, and this is the second answer of Tosafos Eruvin daf 10; and Levush's view appears like the first answer there that even in a wall mashehu suffices; and so appears in Avodat HaKodesh daf 6; and Rashba is worthy to rely on his ruling; and not like Bach who was stringent even with pasin at a tefach and relied on R' Yehonatan — but it is not so, for even R' Yehonatan spoke only regarding a wall; and also regarding a wall one may say he did not mean it literally, as Beit Yosef wrote that mashehu suffices:
eliyah-rabbah:3:_: [3] There is not in the breach four tefachim, etc. And it is possible he speaks when the courtyard is wide in the middle and at its end it is short so that in its full width it is not four tefachim wide; but if the entire courtyard is less than four tefachim no correction is required as written in seif 21 (Magen Avraham); and it is not clear, for there he speaks of a mavo but in a courtyard correction is required as explained in Eruvin daf 12; and so appears in Mordechai and Agudah and Hagahot Alfasi there. For tzurat hapetach see siman 362 seif 10:
eliyah-rabbah:4:_: [4] [Levush] All that it is. Even less than a finger (Beit Yosef):
eliyah-rabbah:5:_: [5] If a person tied, etc. He speaks where they did not inform him — if so he will leave from there — therefore it requires being tied (Magen Avraham); and see siman 362 s.k. 11:
eliyah-rabbah:6:_: [6] [Levush] And specifically in correction, etc. And Melo L'Yom Tov answered that two winds are different; and see s.k. 2:
eliyah-rabbah:7:_: [7] Cannot stand, etc. And even if the wind does not knock it down but only shakes it as explained at the beginning of siman 362 (Magen Avraham):
eliyah-rabbah:8:_: [8] Distant, etc. For the air comes, etc. — therefore if the lechi is wider than three it is permitted since the standing exceeds the breach (Riaz); but the view of Tosafos is that even so it is forbidden (Magen Avraham) — requires study:
eliyah-rabbah:9:_: [9] [Levush] Therefore, etc. And Taz disagrees with Rama that in Terumat HaDeshen it implies specifically with tzurat hapetach that one needs only one reed from here and one reed suffices with all that it is, and not with lechi; and there is no difficulty, for Beit Yosef also holds that with lechi all that it is suffices as above; and Melo L'Yom Tov wrote that Beit Yosef's view is that in every lechi all that it is suffices — nevertheless with smeared plaster he is uncertain; and it appears to me that for Rama it is obvious to him from that which broken fragments — until here, in She'erit Knesset HaGedolah it is explained that they practice even with lechi that one may be more lenient with plaster smearing on lechi than with tzurat hapetach, and they practice to be lenient in both; and it is obvious the plaster should be somewhat thick like the thread of a cloak. Stones protruding from the fence one above the other less than three constitute a lechi when between all of them there is height of ten tefachim (Avodat HaKodesh):
eliyah-rabbah:10:_: [10] [Levush] If he kneaded, etc. So Beit Yosef wrote — and I wonder it was hidden from him the mishnah at the end of Temurah and Yoreh De'ah siman 244 that ashes of asherah wood are forbidden in benefit — if so one must scatter them to the wind like the wood itself (Taz); and see siman 506 seif 3 — requires study; also it appears to me mitzvot are not for benefit were given, and asherah wood itself is forbidden and stands to be burned, and ashes stand to be scattered to the wind — nevertheless:
eliyah-rabbah:11:_: [11] [Levush] First form, second form, third form, fourth form. For Chokhmat Shlomo the third form does not exist, for he wrote inside that for everyone it does not exist (Melo L'Yom Tov); and see Taz and Nachalat Tzvi:
eliyah-rabbah:12:_: [12] [Levush] A tree that was planted, etc. And the same law applies if it grew by itself (Avodat HaKodesh):
eliyah-rabbah:13:_: [13] As if they leaned, etc. It implies that if explicitly they did not lean on it — such as they did not carry on the past Shabbat through this lechi — it is not a lechi (Magen Avraham); and it appears to me specifically when they did not carry on the past Shabbat at all, for there was no other lechi there:
eliyah-rabbah:14:_: [14] [Levush] For the breach is greater, etc. If the side is more than four and we are uncertain whether it stands in the partition on half or more than the breach — if it is not as breached it is permitted, for a doubt in their words is to be lenient; and further there are two sides to be lenient — perhaps the standing is greater; and if you say it is not greater — one may say perhaps like Avodat HaKodesh daf 5:
eliyah-rabbah:15:_: [15] And equal from inside, etc. But in Tosafos daf 9 and Rosh they proved that in this case it is not a lechi, for it is not called visible from outside except to those standing behind the mavo; but in truth Beit Yosef does not explain thus for Tosafos and Rosh; and nevertheless Chokhmat Shlomo explained thus, and so it appears (Melo L'Yom Tov):
eliyah-rabbah:16:_: [16] [Levush] For such is the law in every lechi, etc. It is difficult from siman 365 seif 4; and one must say here he speaks open to karmelit — requires study; and in Shulchan Aruch Magen Avraham wrote that the other side is shorter than this, and in the Gemara he speaks where the other side is also long — until here; and at first glance in every lechi its other side is short and even so it is permitted — requires study:
eliyah-rabbah:17:_: [17] [Levush] And if it is wide four amot, etc. And the same law if he paved with lechayim less less than three — the paving extends four amot; and specifically when the outer lechi does not protrude at all; but when it protrudes somewhat outside the mavo it is permitted. If they were distant from each other three tefachim — one may use until the outer end of the outer lechi; and if each lechi stands, etc. (Avodat HaKodesh daf 6):
eliyah-rabbah:18:_: [18] If he drove in, etc. Specifically when he drove within the thickness of the wall and they protrude outward; but adjacent to the wall it is permitted by reason of lechi (Olat Shabbat):
eliyah-rabbah:19:_: [19] To receive, etc. Meaning if the mavo is wide ten amot it must receive eighteen bricks which is nine amot as written in seif 25 (Avodat HaKodesh). Beit Yosef and Bach wrote: if he made a reed and reeds even if fit to receive a brick it is forbidden since most reeds and reeds are not fit — a mavo open from two sides that was corrected on one side with tzurat hapetach and on one side the two sides of the mavo were not equal but one short and one long — lechi suffices (R' Levi ben Chaviv section 6):
eliyah-rabbah:20:_: [20] A tefach and not in their length three tefachim, etc. For then the korah is as lavud as written in seif 25; and likewise if there is a tefach it is as a korah — see there:
eliyah-rabbah:21:_: [21] There are those who say that it is required, etc. So ruled Rambam and Semag, and so ruled in Avodat HaKodesh; and in Shiltei Giborim it implies this is also Rif's view:
eliyah-rabbah:22:_: [22] And it does not touch, etc. Even if distant from the two walls — such as he drove any amount of reed in the middle of the mavo to place korah on it — for we say lavud from two winds (first chapter of Eruvin):
eliyah-rabbah:23:_: [23] And there are those who say that it is required, etc. So Beit Yosef and Shulchan Aruch wrote; and in my humble opinion those who say do not disagree with the first explanation — for if both have width of a tefach it is permitted whenever between them is less than three; but when both have only width of half a tefach then between them should be only a tefach so that one can place on them a brick which is a tefach and a half — then one finger rests on each korah; and even though a korah needs only a tefach — here where in the two korot themselves there is not a tefach and a tefach between them — two korot are required; and so appears to me the explanation of Tur and R' Yehonatan; and so is proven in Avodat HaKodesh daf 5 — and it is clear; also Bach and the later authorities did not address this; and what Bach was stringent that we require specifically that both have width of a tefach and touch one another literally — this does not appear so in the poskim; and likewise Nachalat Tzvi disagrees with him:
eliyah-rabbah:24:_: [24] Within a tefach. And even if together they are four — if the air between them is four tefachim it does not help, for in any case it is not fit to place a brick on them — unlike in seif 14 where it is fit only that they are not strong (Magen Avraham); and it appears to me there is a scribe's error in his words and one must say if the air between them is more than a tefach it does not help — understand well; however I already wrote to be lenient whenever both have width of a tefach if between them is not three tefachim:
eliyah-rabbah:25:_: [25] And there are those who disqualify, etc. And we set it stringently (Bach):
eliyah-rabbah:26:_: [26] A korah wide, etc. Explanation: wide ten tefachim — since it hangs down ten tefachim it leaves the category of korah like a mat, and it is a partition beneath which goats break through and it is forbidden as Rashba wrote — it teaches us it is permitted since the korah is visible and is not covered by a mat — there is korah on it. And what he wrote even if it extends below ten, etc. — meaning one might have said since it hangs below ten from the ground there is no law of korah on it as he concludes. And what Taz wondered on Rashba from seif 12 — it appears to me there is no difficulty, for in a partition more recognition is required than for lechi:
eliyah-rabbah:27:_: [27] Spaced, etc. And in the latter part precise — then we go stringently:
eliyah-rabbah:28:_: [28] Except with tzurat hapetach, etc. And Rambam holds that less than four amot its law is as a courtyard; and it is possible he did not mean tzurat hapetach specifically (Magen Avraham); and it appears to me also when wide more than ten amot and above its law is as a courtyard; and Shulchan Aruch and Levush relied on the amah that wrote at the end of the seif or with a pas, etc., or with tzurat hapetach; and so appears in Avodat HaKodesh daf 4; also Magen Avraham omitted what is written in Shulchan Aruch seif 32:
eliyah-rabbah:29:_: [29] [Levush] That the eye does not rule, etc. And if the korah is wide four and fit to receive plaster it is permitted and not because of recognition but the ceiling descends and closes as long as the opening of the mavo is not more than ten; and so appears to me that if it were wide seven even if not fit it is valid — for whenever its width is four the eye rules over it (Avodat HaKodesh section 4):
eliyah-rabbah:30:_: [30] Building, etc. And the same with earth; and one must beware when trampled by feet that it not diminish from the measure:
eliyah-rabbah:31:_: [31] Until they are open, etc. Rama's gloss was omitted — and even all courtyards open to each other, and there are those who disagree — until here; and perhaps the reason is because Beit Yosef ruled like those who disagree, and stam is according to his explanation that they are not open to each other (Melo L'Yom Tov); and one may wonder on one as great as he that he did not see at the end of this seif that Levush wrote Rama's words as they are also for practical law primarily like the first view as Bach wrote, and likewise regarding houses open to each other; and in Avodat HaKodesh daf 4 — even if each house and house made eruv, there must be in it four amot by four amot or more:
eliyah-rabbah:32:_: [32] That its length is greater, etc. And even all that it is (Avodat HaKodesh). Which is its length of the mavo — the way of its entrance; and what is not the way of its entrance refers to its width, even though its width is greater than its length (there). The gloss that Rama wrote here — Levush wrote at the end of this siman; and Melo L'Yom Tov erred in this and thought he omitted it to expand, and it is for nothing:
eliyah-rabbah:33:_: [33] That there is not in it four, etc. Explanation: in its opening even if inside it is wide four (Beit Yosef); and so appears from R' Yitzchak daf 92 — R' Yosef wrote daf 88 — and specifically in a mavo; but in a courtyard always correction is required; and see s.k. 3:
eliyah-rabbah:34:_: [34] [Levush] That one of its sides, etc. Explanation: its bank is ten high; and specifically when it is adjacent immediately to the head of the mavo; but if the river is distant from the houses ten amot correction is required, for that place is breached; and likewise regarding a garbage heap he speaks when it is ten high; and it appears in Beit Yosef that even if one side is sea and one side garbage heap and one side closed and one side open to reshut ha-rabbim — with lechi or korah it is also permitted according to this view; and Levush set one of its sides — it appears to include even those who say that even so correction is required. Emunat Shmuel siman 40 wrote: a city with a ditch ten deep and four wide surrounding it is as a partition:
eliyah-rabbah:35:_: [35] And there are those who say, etc. And so is the main ruling; and so Bach ruled; and Magen Avraham wrote specifically regarding the sea, but regarding other rivers we are not concerned lest a sandbar rise unless its way is to dry in summer greatly; and if they freeze in rainy season the partition is nullified and it is forbidden to carry; and Taz expanded that since their way is to freeze they are forbidden forever; and in the Talmud he speaks of a sea whose way is not to freeze; and see Magen Avraham siman 365 s.k. 9:
eliyah-rabbah:36:_: [36] [Levush] And they would carry from the mavo, etc. This is the wording of Melo L'Yom Tov — so Beit Yosef wrote in the name of the Maggid; but Rashi explained they would carry in the mavo itself; and Beit Yosef and Levush omitted Rashi's explanation; and it appears to me the Maggid does not explain that the entire side is sea and also not in width more than ten — therefore he was not concerned to carry in the mavo itself — until here. And it appears to me the Maggid's view that even if dry land slope remains in the depths that is partition as written at the end of this siman — nevertheless it is forbidden lest they carry from mavo to karmelit; and so appears in Magen Avraham; except that what he wrote that for the Maggid tzurat hapetach or lechi or korah does not help — only a complete partition; and in my humble opinion it helps since there is recognition they will not come to carry:
